lesson_title: Angle Sum of Quadrilaterals and Properties of Parallelograms
hook_text: Any quadrilateral tiles a desk. Even the ugly one. Here is why.
clip_script:
The class that tore the corners off triangles is handed a second sheet. Draw any quadrilateral, the teacher says — a boring one, a wild one, anything with four straight sides. Cut it out. Tear off the four corners. Fit them together at a point.

Thirty desks. On every one, the four corners go all the way round: a full turn, no gap, no overlap. The reason is two triangles: draw a diagonal and each half's corners make a half-turn, and two half-turns make a full turn. Then the teacher hands out identical ugly quadrilaterals cut from card, and the class finds that rotating each tile a half-turn against its neighbour makes them cover the desk with no gaps — one of each corner meeting at every point, 360 exactly.
visual_style: Four ragged paper corners sliding together into a full circle, then identical irregular quadrilateral tiles spiralling out to cover the frame with no gaps
pacing: one tear per beat, then a quickening tiling
call_to_action: Open the full session to investigate quadrilateral angles and parallelogram properties and calculate with them.
